answer: The retained passages support cryptocurrency’s capacity to be trust property, but make actual ownership depend on the particular relationship, applicable terms and customer consent. They distinguish non-consenting customers’ pooled beneficial interests from other customers’ rights, BlueFire’s accounts, ETD holders’ claims and Samara’s unsuccessful trust claim. They do not establish a trust or fulfillment of regulatory responsibility for a Product Provider under 26EC22. That transfer requires an applicable legal rule, a justified analogy and actual product and relationship facts. Scenario seven remains textually unresolved, and complete subsequent treatment is unknown.

claims.inference: Text: capacity to be trust property is distinct from the existence of a particular trust. The conclusion preserves the non-consenting-customer exception.
missing_premises: For another customer or product: applicable contractual terms, consent evidence, relevant property and the facts establishing the required trust certainties.
claims.proposition: The 2023 conclusion treats cryptocurrency as property capable of being held on trust, but rejects a trust under the 2018 terms for customers subject to those terms.
claims.status: supported by retained conclusion; application conditional

support.quote: Cryptocurrency is “property” and is capable of being held on trust
Except the Non-Consenting Customers, the 2018 T&C applied to, and governed the relationship between all the Customers
However, the terms of the 2018 T&C show that there was no certainty of intention to create a trust over the cryptocurrencies held by Gatecoin

claims.inference: Text: the 2023 reasons quote principles attributed to Briggs J in Re Lehman Brothers. Deduction: labels and intermediary roles cannot replace assessment of the actual agreement and relationship.
missing_premises: The complete agreement and objectively relevant relationship facts for each pair of parties.
Full reasons and authority analysis before treating the quoted principles as a fully verified transferable ratio.
claims.proposition: Trust, custody and ownership terminology, or an agency or brokerage relationship, is not conclusive of beneficial ownership.
claims.status: supported quoted reasoning; transfer requires analysis

support.quote: The words used by the parties such as ‘trust’, ‘custody’, ‘belonging’, ‘ownership’, ‘title’, may be persuasive, but they are not conclusive in favour of the recognition of B’s proprietary interest in the property, if the terms of the agreement or relationship, viewed objectively, compel a different conclusion.

The identification of a relationship in which A is B’s agent or broker is not conclusive of a conclusion that A is, in relation to the property, B’s trustee, although it may be a pointer towards that conclusion.

claims.inference: Text: paragraph 8 differentiates automated activity from customer access or use, and provides evidential qualifications. Deduction: a post-date ledger entry alone does not settle consent.
missing_premises: Customer-specific access, use and instruction evidence, including timing and transaction category.
The complete NCC definition and relevant procedural directions.
claims.proposition: The 2025 reasoning makes customer classification depend on the circumstances of transactions, rather than merely their recording after the relevant date.
claims.status: supported for stated scenarios; incomplete classifier

support.quote: The customers should be regarded as NCCs unless there is evidence to show that they have accessed or used the Platform to effect the transactions

The transactions described in the 5th to 6th scenarios on their face required the customers to access or use the Platform to effect them and, prima facie, the customers fall outside the definition of NCC.
However, if the customers are able to prove that they gave the instruction to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

claims.inference: Text: the retained 2025 passages state distinct results for distinct parties. Deduction: neither account attribution nor ownership treatment can be generalized across those relationships.
missing_premises: The underlying reasons and facts for each relationship before extending these conclusions beyond these proceedings.
claims.proposition: NCCs’ pooled beneficial ownership, BlueFire-account assets, ETD claims and Samara’s creditor status must remain separate.
claims.status: supported by retained summary and disposition

support.quote: Each NCC is a beneficial tenant-in-common in a pool of cryptocurrency and fiat currency.
The Currencies recorded in BlueFire’s accounts are assets of Gatecoin.
ETD represents a cause of action by ETD Holder against Gatecoin for breach of trust.
Gatecoin does not hold the Subject Bitcoins or the Specified Account on trust for Mr Samara.
Mr Samara is only an unsecured creditor to the extent of his claim less the amount he already received through execution of the HCA Judgment.

claims.inference: Comparison of text: paragraph 8 rejects scenario seven’s factual existence, while paragraph 95 includes it within a conditional exception. The annexure separately specifies categories and proof requirements. No priority or harmonization is established here.
missing_premises: Full reasons, operative order and any clarification reconciling paragraphs 8 and 95 with the annexure.
claims.proposition: Scenario seven cannot safely be encoded as a settled automatic classification.

support.quote: The transactions described in the 7th scenario did not exist and the customers should not be regarded as NCC.

The 5th to 7th scenarios prima facie fall outside the definition of NCC but if the customers can prove that they gave the relevant instructions to Gatecoin before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

Any Customer who claims to have transactions enumerated in paragraphs 1.2(b) shall notify the Liquidators and provide evidence to the Liquidators in support of such a claim within 21 days from the date hereof.

claims.inference: Deduction: Gatecoin’s ownership analysis may inform identification of the interests that records must reflect. Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 separately address retained regulatory responsibility despite outsourcing. Neither establishes that the Product Provider is necessarily a trustee or that responsibility has been fulfilled.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained 26EC22 edition to the entity, product, activity and assessment period, including conditions and amendments.
Proof of Product Provider status and the actual outsourcing and authority arrangements.
A legally justified transfer of the relevant Gatecoin proposition, accounting for the exchange-insolvency context and materially different product relationships.
Governing law, constitutive documents, customer terms and consent, asset identification, title structure and settlement arrangements.
An applicable fulfillment standard and evidence of actual supervision, operational soundness and proper ownership records throughout the relevant period.
claims.proposition: Applying Gatecoin to a Product Provider requires separate ownership, regulatory-applicability and fulfillment analyses.
claims.status: reasoned conditional proposal; fulfillment not established

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: Text supports the 2025 court’s express recording of the earlier conclusions. Judgment: this is narrower than certifying complete subsequent treatment or independently verifying the candidate’s treatment label.
missing_premises: Complete subsequent judicial treatment, appeals and any relevant qualifications.
claims.proposition: The 2025 passage records the 2023 conclusions; the supplied material does not establish complete later treatment.

rival_readings: Scenario seven: paragraph 8 supports factual absence and exclusion from NCC status; paragraph 95 facially permits the instruction-based exception for scenarios five to seven. The annexure does not resolve that tension on the supplied text.

Transfer to 26EC22: Gatecoin may inform analysis of the ownership interests requiring records, but treating its customer-specific trust findings as determining every Product Provider’s title or regulatory fulfillment is unsupported.
unresolved: Full reasons and application have not been independently checked; retained passages are selected extracts.
